newsitem.title: USA: U.S. pork industry launches promotion campaign.
newsitem.headline: U.S. pork industry launches promotion campaign.

text.p: October is National Pork Month and the National Pork Producers Council has unveiled three major supermarket pork promotions, said Mike Laurent, NPPC director of retail marketing.

Pork Lover's Breakfast, which runs through November, promotes breakfast meats -- ham, sausage and bacon. Selected meat items featured in the promotion will be displayed in meat cases with a logo of a frying pan.
"We will be offering incentives to retailers to feature breakfast pork items more often in their ads at a reduced price," Laurent said.
The HAMS (How America Makes Sandwiches) promotion will focus on supermarkets' delicatessen and specialty hams, targeting use in school lunches and cool weather meals.
Handouts for customers will include ham recipes and consumer tips on carving and serving, he said.
Another planned promotion is called "Rack of Pork, The Next Tradition." Rack of Pork, a new cut developed by the industry, is a family-sized pork crown roast.
Laurent called it a top-of-the-line pork cut.
"We are getting a fantastic response from retailers and packers," Laurent said.

The Rack of Pork promotion is geared to run through the Christmas holidays. It will include ads in magazines and on national television this fall. The print ads will deliver a recipe for Rack of Pork and will run in Ladies' Home Journal, People, Good Housekeeping, Bon Appetit and other magazines.

The NPPC has earmarked $6.75 million for the pork promotions this fall out of a yearly promotion and advertising budget of 27 million that is funded through the pork producer checkoff program, said NPPC spokesman Charles Harness.
